A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with matching core loss, theoretical results and experiments. Their main texts and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial retitling, reorganization and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, plus an untrained-model analysis on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 in Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds SAOCP and local-coverage evaluations in Figure 2 and estimated-noise-rate results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The robust pinball loss and its constant/dynamic single-threshold updates are unchanged. However, v3 adds NR-SAOCP and NR-SF-OGD in Appendix D: multiple active experts, threshold aggregation, robust-loss-based expert weighting and gradient-normalized updates. This substantially extends the proposed procedure beyond the original threshold-update algorithm.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100, ImageNet and the appendix's CIFAR-10 coverage are retained. Appendix C adds an evaluation scenario where the noise rate is unknown and estimated. CIFAR-10 itself is not a new dataset; v1 already used it for the untrained-model analysis.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 2 adds comparisons against SAOCP using standard pinball loss, with noisy-label and clean-label controls. The constant- and dynamic-rate baselines remain; calling them ACI clarifies the identity of methods already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v3 adds local coverage evaluated with window length L = 200. Appendix C introduces a noise-estimation testing procedure at noise rates 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3. The retained classifier training recipes, score functions, and constant/dynamic learning-rate schedules are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends the analysis to two practical questions: coverage over local time intervals rather than only long-run averages, and robustness when the supplied noise rate is estimated incorrectly. These appear in Figure 2 and Appendix C. The untrained-model analysis remains, while v1 Appendix B.5's dynamic-rate noise-sensitivity curves in Figure 4 are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Averaging across score functions in Table 1 is retained and does not constitute repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched detailed tables, v1 Tables 3–9 versus v3 Tables 2–8, have identical numerical results. Substantive new findings concern SAOCP, local coverage and estimated noise rates: v3 Table 9 reports coverage gaps of 6.99% versus 0.82% for baseline versus proposed method when the true rate is 0.1 and its estimate is 0.09. v1's ImageNet Figure 2 trajectories, Figure 4 and distinct results in its architecture-summary Table 2 are removed.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 4.1, Remark 4.2 and Appendix D.1's noise-gap analysis for the uncorrected dynamic-rate baseline are removed. The loss-unbiasedness results, robust constant/dynamic coverage bounds, regret analysis and threshold-convergence analysis remain mathematically unchanged after matching their new numbering and locations.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on NR-OCP with constant and dynamic learning rates. v3 broadens the central contribution to a robust loss complementary to multiple existing online conformal algorithms, explicitly including SAOCP and empirical local-coverage performance. The core uniform-noise, unbiasedness and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new results as evidence of applicability when noise rates are imperfectly estimated and of versatility across online conformal algorithms. These extend v1's interpretations, while the formal limitation to uniform noise with a known rate remains explicitly stated.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds implementation guidance through two algorithms, including expert initialization with learning rate 1/sqrt(3), threshold inheritance, weighting and gradient normalization. Appendix C identifies Li et al. (2021) as the noise-estimation procedure. Existing classifier-training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work survey and comparison with Einbinder et al. are largely retained. v3 adds Jun et al. (2017) on coin betting and Orabona and Pál (2018) on scale-free learning, and emphasizes complementarity with existing conformal methods in its positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion are rewritten around the robust loss. Separate constant/dynamic results sections become a noise-impact section and a unified method section; experiments gain explicit setup/results subsections, and proofs are consolidated into Appendix E. Several cross-references become unresolved.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 2 becomes a six-panel display of long-run and local coverage; v1 Figure 4 and its architecture-summary Table 2 disappear, while v3 adds an estimated-noise table and two algorithm displays. Retained tables are resized and repacked. A proof equation on v3 page 24 extends beyond the page edge.

improvement.justification: The SAOCP adaptation, local-coverage evaluation and estimated-noise experiment provide useful applicability evidence absent from v1, with added algorithm details supporting reproducibility. The gains are limited by removal of the dynamic-baseline theorem and supporting analysis, plus new unresolved cross-references and a clipped equation. The core method, most theory and matched numerical results remain stable, making the net improvement modest.
